cells.reason: Hoboken has a long-standing municipal rent control ordinance (Hoboken City Code ch. 155). NJ leaves rent control to municipalities, and the code is published on ecode360.
cells.quoted_span: Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.

rule.conflict_note: Exact cap formula, exemptions and unit thresholds not confirmed from a provided document; state law exempts newly constructed multiple dwellings from local rent control for 30 years (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5).
rule.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt for 30 years under state law; subsidized housing may be exempt.
rule.interaction: NJ has no state rent cap; local ordinance is the only rent control.
rule.key_value: Municipal rent control limits annual rent increases
rule.quoted_span: Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.
rule.requirement: Hoboken limits rent increases on covered units under its municipal rent control ordinance; check with the Hoboken rent control office whether your unit is covered.
rule.title: Hoboken Rent Control Ordinance

cells.reason: State Anti-Eviction Act clearly applies. Hoboken may have local eviction or relocation provisions, but nothing provided confirms them.

cells.reason: The $50 application fee cap is a state law (P.L.2025, c.405); no separate Hoboken fee rule is shown.
cells.quoted_span: A landlord, or agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which exceeds $50.

cells.reason: Criminal-history and source-of-income screening limits come from state law (Fair Chance in Housing Act, LAD); no Hoboken-specific rule is shown.
cells.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
